title: Money
about: Collocations for everyday money: spending, saving and wasting it, talking about prices that go up and down, and earning and making money, such as squander money, rock-bottom prices, money is tight and make a small fortune.

items.pattern: spend money / £20 / a fortune on sth · spend – spent – spent · spend money on doing sth
items.meaning: use money to pay for things
items.example: We **spend too much money on** takeaways.
more: My son **spends** all his pocket **money on** sweets and football stickers.
I **spent** £60 **on** a present for my sister's birthday.
items.watchOut: «Витрачати на щось» — spend on: I spent £60 on a present. Spend for тут звучить неприродно. Spend — неправильне дієслово: spend – spent – spent.

items.pattern: save money (for sth / to do sth) · save up (for sth) · save money on sth (= pay less)
items.meaning: keep money instead of spending it so that you can use it later; also pay less than usual for something
items.example: I take sandwiches to work to **save money**.
more: My daughter is **saving** her birthday **money** for a new bike.
You can **save money on** train tickets if you book early.
items.watchOut: «Відкладати гроші» — save (up) або put money aside, а не put off money (put off — відкласти на потім) і не collect money (collect — збирати гроші з інших людей). «Економити на чомусь» — save money on sth.

items.pattern: waste / squander money (on sth) · a waste of money · squander is stronger, for large sums
items.meaning: spend money badly, on things that are not worth it; squander means wasting a large amount, often all you have
items.example: Don't **waste money on** cheap umbrellas: they break in the first strong wind.
more: The club **squandered** millions on players who hardly ever played.
That gym membership was a complete **waste of money**: I went twice.
items.watchOut: «Змарнувати гроші» — waste money, а не lose money: lose money — втратити гроші (наприклад, на невдалій угоді). Squander кажуть про великі суми: squander an inheritance, squander a fortune.

items.pattern: change money · change pounds into / for euros · also exchange money
items.meaning: swap the money of one country for the money of another
items.example: Don't forget to **change** some **money** before we cross the border.
more: Can I **change** these dollars **for** Polish złoty here?
The rate is usually better if you **change money** in town.
items.watchOut: «Поміняти долари на євро» — change dollars into / for euros, а не on euros. Пункт обміну валют — a bureau de change. Не плутай: change — це ще й «решта»: Keep the change.

items.pattern: throw (your) money around / about · informal
items.meaning: spend a lot of money carelessly, often to show people that you have it
items.example: My cousin **throws his money around** as if he's a millionaire, but he's always borrowing from his mum.
more: When he got his first wages, he **threw his money around** on taxis and designer trainers.
Rich tourists **throwing their money about** have made the town very expensive.
items.watchOut: Не плутай із throw money away — викинути гроші на вітер, просто змарнувати. Throw money around — витрачати бездумно й напоказ. Британці кажуть і throw money about.

items.pattern: throw money at a problem / sth · informal, critical
items.meaning: spend a lot of money, often more than necessary, trying to solve a problem, usually without real success
items.example: Our old car breaks down every month, and we keep **throwing money at it**.
more: The council **threw money at** the town centre, but the shops are still empty.
**Throwing money at** a leaking roof won't help if nobody finds the cause.
items.watchOut: Прийменник at: throw money at the problem, а не on і не to. Вираз критичний: грошей багато, а користі мало.

items.pattern: donate money / £10 / clothes to a charity / a hospital · make a donation
items.meaning: give money to a charity or an organisation to help other people
items.example: Every Christmas my grandparents **donate money to** a children's hospital.
more: The football club **donated** £5,000 **to** the new playground.
You can **donate** online or put cash in the box by the door.
items.watchOut: «Пожертвувати гроші» — donate money, а не sacrifice: sacrifice — пожертвувати чимось своїм заради мети (sacrifice your free time). Кому — зазвичай to: donate to charity.

items.pattern: high / low prices · prices are high / low · a high / low price (for sth)
items.meaning: prices that are a lot of money or not much money; English talks about prices as up or down, like height
items.example: The hotel shop has really **high prices**, so we buy water at the supermarket.
more: The market has **low prices** because it sells straight from the farms.
The village shop charges **high prices** because it's the only one for miles.
items.watchOut: «Дорогі ціни» — high prices; expensive prices звучить неприродно, бо expensive і cheap кажуть про самі речі: The shoes were expensive. «Дешеві ціни» — краще low prices (cheap prices чути хіба що в рекламі).

items.pattern: rock-bottom prices · at rock-bottom prices · prices hit rock bottom · mostly in adverts
items.meaning: extremely low prices, as low as they can go
items.example: The furniture shop is closing down and selling everything at **rock-bottom prices**.
more: I bought my winter coat at a **rock-bottom price** in the January sales.
The sign in the window said: '**Rock-bottom prices**! Everything must go!'
items.watchOut: Перед іменником — через дефіс: rock-bottom prices. Без іменника — два слова: Prices have hit rock bottom.

items.pattern: prices go up / rise / increase (by 10% / to £3) · rise – rose – risen · a price rise / increase
items.meaning: prices become higher
items.example: The **price** of a bus ticket **has gone up** twice this year.
more: Electricity **prices rose** sharply last winter.
Ticket **prices** always **increase** in the summer holidays.
items.watchOut: «Ціни ростуть» — у розмові найчастіше prices are rising / going up. Rise — без додатка: prices rise. А «підняти ціни» — raise prices: The shop raised its prices. Тому prices are rising, а не raising.

items.pattern: prices soar · soaring prices · soar – soared
items.meaning: prices go up very fast to a very high level
items.example: When the storm ruined the harvest, the price of tomatoes **soared**.
more: Rents have **soared** in our area, so many young families are moving out.
Concert ticket **prices** have **soared**: my daughter paid £120 for one show.
items.watchOut: «Ціни злетіли» — prices soared (або shot up), а не flew up. Вимова: soar звучить так само, як sore і saw: /sɔː/.

items.pattern: prices go down / fall / come down / drop · fall – fell – fallen · a fall in prices
items.meaning: prices become lower
items.example: The **price** of strawberries **goes down** in June, when they're in season.
more: When the new supermarket opened, **prices** at the old one **fell** too.
We're waiting for house **prices** to **come down** before we buy.
items.watchOut: Lower і reduce зазвичай потребують додатка: the shop lowered / reduced its prices (магазин знизив ціни). Про самі ціни кажуть go down / fall / drop, а не prices lowered.

items.pattern: reasonably priced (food / hotels) · a reasonable price · reasonable prices
items.meaning: not too cheap and not too expensive; at a fair price
items.example: The café near the museum is **reasonably priced**, and the soup is excellent.
more: We found a **reasonably priced** flat ten minutes from the beach.
The taxis in this town are **reasonably priced**, so we didn't hire a car.
items.watchOut: «Нормальна ціна» — a reasonable / fair price, а не normal price (normal price — звичайна ціна, без знижки). «Адекватна ціна» — теж reasonable, а не adequate. Перед priced — прислівник: reasonably priced, а не reasonable priced.

items.pattern: a ridiculous price · for / at a ridiculous price · ridiculously cheap / expensive
items.meaning: a price that is surprising because it is much too high or much too low
items.uk: смішна (надто низька) або шалена (надто висока) ціна
items.example: They wanted £8 for a cup of coffee: what a **ridiculous price**!
more: Twenty pounds for a whole sofa? That's a **ridiculous price**: there must be something wrong with it.
Parking at the hospital is **ridiculously expensive**.
items.watchOut: «Смішна ціна» — a ridiculous price, а не a funny price. Ridiculous може означати і надто дорого, і надто дешево: це видно з контексту.

items.pattern: money is tight · money's a bit tight (at the moment)
items.meaning: there isn't much money, so you have to be careful how you spend it
items.example: When we first moved to the city, **money was tight**, so we walked everywhere.
more: **Money is** always a bit **tight** after Christmas.
My grandparents brought up five children when **money was tight**, and they never wasted food.
items.watchOut: «У нас туго з грошима» — money is tight (підмет — money), а не it's tight with money. Ще кажуть: we're short of money.

items.pattern: be in short supply · sth is in short supply
items.meaning: there isn't enough of something
items.example: Good builders are **in short supply**, so we waited months for ours.
more: Before the storm, bread and bottled water were **in short supply** in every shop.
Patience is **in short supply** in our house at seven in the morning.
items.watchOut: «У дефіциті» — in short supply. Deficit англійською — переважно про бюджет (a budget deficit), а не про товари в магазині. Іноді чути in low supply, але сталий вираз — in short supply.

items.pattern: a steady / regular / stable income · have / need a steady income
items.meaning: money that you receive regularly, so you know how much will come in
items.example: Renting out the spare room gives my parents a **steady income**.
more: A small shop on a busy street can give you a **steady income** for years.
After years of odd jobs, she wanted work with a **steady income** and paid holidays.
items.watchOut: «Стабільний дохід» — a steady / regular / stable income. Firm і strong з income у цьому значенні зазвичай не вживають.

items.pattern: earn / get / be on a good / high / decent salary
items.meaning: be paid a lot of money for your job (a salary is usually paid every month)
items.example: My brother **earns a good salary**, but the rent takes half of it.
more: Her new job is boring, but she **earns a good salary**.
Pilots **earn** a very **good salary**, but they're often away from home.
items.watchOut: «Хороша, висока зарплата» — a good / high salary; big salary — розмовно. Salary — щомісячна (річна) зарплата; оплату за годину чи за тиждень називають wages. Вимова earn — /ɜːn/, як urn.

items.pattern: make / earn big money · informal
items.meaning: earn a lot of money (informal)
items.example: Footballers in the top league **make big money**, even in their first season.
more: My cousin went to work on the oil rigs, and now he's **making big money**.
Nobody **makes big money** working in a bookshop, but I love it.
items.watchOut: «Великі гроші» — big money; large money звучить неприродно. Вираз розмовний; у формальному тексті — earn a lot of money / a high income.

items.pattern: seriously rich · informal · also really / extremely / very rich
items.meaning: very rich (informal)
items.example: You have to be **seriously rich** to buy a house on that street.
more: Her husband's family is **seriously rich**: they own half the hotels on the coast.
He isn't **seriously rich**, he just likes expensive watches.
items.watchOut: Absolutely і utterly ставлять перед «крайніми» прикметниками (absolutely exhausted), тому absolutely rich чи utterly rich звучать неприродно. Strongly rich — калька. Кажуть seriously / really / extremely rich.

items.pattern: make / earn money (from sth / by doing sth) · make money also = make a profit
items.meaning: get money by working, selling things or running a business
items.example: My son **makes money** by washing the neighbours' cars at the weekend.
more: I **earned** my first **money** delivering newspapers at six in the morning.
How do street musicians **make money** if most people just walk past?
items.watchOut: «Заробляти» — make або earn money, а не win money: win — виграти (у лотерею, у конкурсі). Earn — переважно за власну роботу; make — ширше: робота, продаж, бізнес.

items.pattern: make a withdrawal (from your account) · formal · informal: withdraw money, take money out
items.meaning: take money out of your bank account
items.example: You'll need your passport to **make a withdrawal** at the counter.
more: My grandmother still goes into the bank to **make a withdrawal** every Friday.
I **withdrew** £50 from the cash machine for the taxi.
items.watchOut: «Зняти гроші» — make a withdrawal (офіційно), withdraw money або просто take money out. Не do a withdrawal і не take off money: take off — зняти одяг. Протилежне — make a deposit, pay money in.

items.pattern: raise money (for sth / to do sth) · raise – raised – raised · raise money for charity
items.meaning: collect or get money for a particular purpose, for example from other people, events or a bank
items.example: Our neighbours ran a marathon to **raise money for** the local hospice.
more: We're **raising money** to repair the church roof.
My uncle **raised** the **money** for his first van by selling his motorbike.
items.watchOut: Raise (з додатком) — зібрати гроші: raise money. Rise — без додатка: prices rise. Тому raise money, а не rise money. Кальку gather money зазвичай не вживають; collect money — коли збирають готівку в людей (у скриньку, у конверт).

items.pattern: get a (really) good deal (on sth) · informal · = get a bargain
items.meaning: buy something for a good price, cheaper than usual
items.example: We **got a really good deal** on our holiday by booking in January.
more: The man at the market gave us **a good deal** because we bought three rugs.
Ask at the desk: students often **get a good deal** on gym membership.
items.watchOut: «Вигідна покупка» — a good deal або a bargain, а не a profitable agreement. Deal тут — не «справа» й не договір, а покупка за вигідною ціною.

items.pattern: be going cheap · informal
items.meaning: being sold at a low price, often because the seller wants to get rid of it quickly
items.example: Christmas decorations are always **going cheap** in January.
more: There's a piano **going cheap** on our street: the family are moving abroad.
Tickets for tonight's match are **going cheap** online because it's raining.
items.watchOut: Тут cheap, а не cheaply: is going cheap. Вираз розмовний; нейтрально — is on sale at a low price.

items.pattern: make a small fortune · cost / spend a small fortune · informal
items.meaning: make a lot of money ('small' is a joke: it actually means a lot)
items.example: Her grandad **made a small fortune** selling ice cream on the beach every summer.
more: Our wedding **cost a small fortune**, but it was worth every penny.
He **made a small fortune** selling second-hand cars.
items.watchOut: A small fortune — це не «маленькі гроші», а дуже багато: small тут жартівливе. «Статок» — fortune, а не state чи condition.

items.phrase: money is tied up in sth
items.pattern: money is tied up in sth (a house, a business) · tie up money in sth
items.meaning: money that you can't use or spend because it is in a house, a business, a long-term account, etc.
items.example: My **money is tied up in** a savings account until next year, so I can't touch it.
more: They have **money tied up in** two holiday flats, but very little cash.
Don't **tie up** all your **money in** one house: keep some for emergencies.
items.watchOut: Коли гроші «заморожені» у твоєму будинку чи бізнесі, кажуть money is tied up in sth. Frozen — коли рахунок заблокував банк чи держава (frozen bank accounts).

warmup.uk: Скільки ти витрачаєш на їжу щотижня?
warmup.q: How much do you spend ___ food every week?
warmup.explain: Витрачати гроші на щось — spend money on sth, з прийменником on.

warmup.uk: Після повені багато людей пожертвували гроші сім'ям, які втратили домівки.
warmup.q: After the floods, lots of people ___ money to families who had lost their homes.
warmup.explain: Жертвувати гроші — donate (to). Sacrifice — пожертвувати чимось своїм заради мети (часом, здоров'ям).

warmup.uk: У цьому кафе дуже високі ціни.
warmup.explain: Ціни бувають high або low. Expensive і cheap кажуть про самі речі: an expensive café.
Ціни ростуть — prices are rising (going up). Raise потребує додатка: the shop is raising its prices. Arise — виникати (про проблему, питання).

warmup.uk: П'ять фунтів за шкіряні черевики — це смішна ціна!
warmup.q: Five pounds for leather boots is a ___ price!
warmup.explain: Смішна ціна — a ridiculous price. Comic — комічний (про фільм, актора); funny price — хіба що «дивна» ціна, а не абсурдно низька чи висока.
З грошима туго — money is tight (буквально «тісно»).

warmup.uk: Банкомат зламався, тож доведеться зняти гроші в касі.
warmup.q: The cash machine is broken, so I'll have to ___ at the counter.
warmup.explain: Зняти гроші з рахунку — make a withdrawal (офіційно) або take money out. Take off — зняти одяг.

warmup.uk: Нова кухня коштувала нам цілий статок.
warmup.q: The new kitchen cost us a small ___.
warmup.explain: Цілий статок — a small fortune: small тут жартівливе, насправді це дуже багато. State — держава або стан.

A.q: Those cheap shoes fell apart after a week: I really ___ my money.
A.explain: Waste money — змарнувати гроші. Save — заощадити, raise — зібрати гроші на якусь мету.

A.q: The bank on the high street will ___ your dollars into pounds without a fee.
A.explain: Обміняти валюту — change (або exchange) money: change dollars into pounds.

A.q: The hotel has thrown money ___ its restaurant, but the food is still terrible.
A.explain: Throw money at sth — заливати щось грошима, а користі мало. Прийменник at.

B.q: After the new railway line opened, house prices in the village ___.
B.explain: Ціни злетіли — prices soared. Fly — літати, про ціни так не кажуть; raise потребує додатка (raise prices).

B.q: The travel agent near us sells last-minute holidays at ___ prices.
B.explain: Найнижчі ціни — rock-bottom prices (rock bottom — «кам'яне дно»). Small prices — калька з «маленьких цін».

B.q: The bike shop on our street is friendly and ___ priced.
B.explain: За помірною ціною — reasonably priced. Normally priced — за звичайною ціною, без знижки.

C.q: My friend's camping gear is ___ cheap: she's decided she hates camping.
The school is ___ money for a new minibus.
C.explain: Зібрати гроші — raise money. Rise — без додатка (prices rise), grow — рости.

C.q: They must be ___ rich: they've got three houses and a boat.
C.explain: Seriously rich — розмовне «страшенно багатий». Absolutely ставлять перед крайніми прикметниками (absolutely exhausted), strongly rich — калька.

example.title: My first car
example.uk:
Коли мені було сімнадцять, удома з грошима було туго, тож на літо я влаштувався в кафе, щоб заробити трохи грошей. Щоп'ятниці я клав зарплату в банк і намагався ніколи не знімати гроші з рахунку. Мої друзі смітили грошима на одяг і концерти, а я відкладав гроші на машину.

У серпні ціни в кафе зросли, а разом із ними й мої чайові. До вересня я назбирав достатньо. Я знайшов стару машину, яку задешево продавали в автомайстерні біля нашого дому. Власник сказав, що це смішна ціна, але йому потрібне було місце. Я знав, що купив її дуже вигідно.

Того літа я не заробив цілого статку, але ще ніколи так не пишався своїми грошима.
example.en:
When I was seventeen, [[money was tight|c1]] at home, so I got a summer job in a café to [[earn some money|c7]]. Every Friday I put my wages in the bank and tried never to [[make a withdrawal|c8]]. My friends were [[throwing their money around|a5]] on clothes and concerts, but I was [[saving money|a2]] for a car.

In August the café's [[prices went up|b3]], and so did my tips. By September I had enough. I found an old car [[going cheap|c11]] at a garage near our house. The owner said it was a [[ridiculous price|b7]], but he needed the space. I knew I had [[got a really good deal|c10]].

I didn't [[make a small fortune|c12]] that summer, but I've never been so proud of my money.
